literal: If a todi of ploughed soil is dried to a quarter-measure, even a handful of manure without needing, abundantly it will yield.
translation: If ploughed soil is dried so thoroughly that a measure of one todi shrinks to a quarter-measure, the land will yield abundantly even without a handful of manure.
modern: உழுத மண்ணின் ஒரு பலம் எடையுள்ள புழுதி, காய்ந்து கால் பலம் எடையாகக் குறையும் அளவுக்குக் காய வைத்தால், ஒரு கைப்பிடி அளவு எருவும் தேவையில்லாமல் பயிர்கள் மிகச் சிறப்பாக விளையும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of thoroughly drying ploughed soil before sowing. The poet uses precise ancient weights: a 'toṭi' (equivalent to a 'palam') and a 'kaḥcu' (one-fourth of a 'toṭi'). If the wet, ploughed soil is left to dry in the sun so intensely that its moisture evaporates completely, reducing its weight to a quarter of its original wet weight, the soil becomes exceptionally fertile. Such well-dried soil becomes so rich in nutrients and aeration that the farmer does not even need to add a single handful of manure ('piṭittu eruvum vēṇṭātu') to get an abundant harvest ('cālap paṭum').
